facts.statement: The broad-billed parrot likely went extinct around the 1680s.
facts.quote: extinct: c. 1680s?

facts.statement: The scientific species name of the broad-billed parrot is mauritianus.
facts.quote: species: mauritianus

facts.statement: The broad-billed parrot was scientifically described by Richard Owen in 1866.
facts.quote: authority: (Owen, 1866)

facts.statement: The broad-billed parrot was endemic to the island of Mauritius in the Mascarene Islands.
facts.quote: It was endemic to the Mascarene island of Mauritius.

facts.statement: Dutch ships' journals from 1598 onwards first referred to the bird as the "Indian raven".
facts.quote: The species was first referred to as the "Indian raven" in Dutch ships' journals from 1598 onwards.

facts.statement: Reports published in 1601 contain the first illustration of the broad-billed parrot, alongside the first illustration of a dodo.
facts.quote: They appear in reports published in 1601, which also contain the first illustration of the bird, along with the first of a dodo.

facts.statement: Dutch sailors categorized the broad-billed parrots separately from parrots, calling them "Indische ravens" without useful descriptions.
facts.quote: The Dutch sailors who visited Mauritius categorised the broad-billed parrots separately from parrots, and referred to them as "Indische ravens" (translated as either "Indian ravens" or "Indian crows") without accompanying useful descriptions

facts.statement: Richard Owen described the first known physical remain, a subfossil mandible, in 1866 and named it Psittacus mauritianus.
facts.quote: The British biologist Richard Owen described the mandible in 1866 and identified it as belonging to a large parrot species, to which he gave the binomial name Psittacus mauritianus.

facts.statement: Richard Owen first used the common name "broad-billed parrot" in a 1866 lecture.
facts.quote: The common name "broad-billed parrot" was first used by Owen in a 1866 lecture.

facts.statement: In 1868, Hermann Schlegel examined an unlabelled sketch in the rediscovered 1601 journal of the ship Gelderland.
facts.quote: In 1868, shortly after the 1601 journal of the Dutch East India Company ship Gelderland had been rediscovered, the German ornithologist Hermann Schlegel examined an unlabelled pen-and-ink sketch in it.

facts.statement: Alfred Newton assigned the bird to its own genus, Lophopsittacus, in 1875 due to differences in bones and crest from Psittacus species.
facts.quote: Because its bones and crest are significantly different from those of Psittacus species, the British zoologist Alfred Newton assigned it to its own genus in 1875, which he called Lophopsittacus.

facts.statement: More fossils were found in 1889 under Theodore Sauzier and described by Edward Newton and Hans Gadow in 1893.
facts.quote: More fossils were found in the swamp under the direction of the French naturalist Theodore Sauzier in 1889, and described by the British ornithologists Edward Newton and Hans Gadow in 1893.

facts.statement: In 2007, Julian Hume reclassified the bird as a species in the genus Psittacula, calling it Thirioux's grey parrot.
facts.quote: In 2007, on the basis of a comparison of subfossils, and correlated with old descriptions of small grey parrots, the British palaeontologist Julian Hume reclassified it as a species in the genus Psittacula and called it Thirioux's grey parrot.

facts.statement: Julian Hume reidentified a skull originally assigned to the Rodrigues parrot as belonging to the broad-billed parrot, making it the second known skull of the species.
facts.quote: Hume also reidentified a skull found by Thirioux that was originally assigned to the Rodrigues parrot (Necropsittacus rodricanus) as belonging to the broad-billed parrot instead, making it only the second skull known of this species.

facts.statement: The broad-billed parrot is classified as a member of the tribe Psittaculini.
facts.quote: It has been classified as a member of the tribe Psittaculini, along with other Mascarene parrots.

facts.statement: Emile Oustalet argued in 1897 and France Staub as late as 1993 that the "Indian raven" was a hornbill, though no hornbill remains have been found on the island.
facts.quote: The French zoologist Emile Oustalet argued in 1897 that the "Indian raven" was a hornbill whose remains awaited discovery. The Mauritian ornithologist France Staub was in favour of this idea as late as 1993.

facts.statement: The taxonomic affinities of the broad-billed parrot remain undetermined.
facts.quote: The taxonomic affinities of the broad-billed parrot are undetermined.

facts.statement: Newton and Gadow thought the broad-billed parrot was closely related to the Rodrigues parrot in 1893 but could not determine if they belonged in the same genus.
facts.quote: Newton and Gadow thought it to be closely related to the Rodrigues parrot in 1893, but were unable to determine whether they both belonged in the same genus, since a crest was only known from the latter.

facts.statement: Graham S. Cowles found the skulls of the broad-billed parrot and Rodrigues parrot too dissimilar to be close relatives in 1987.
facts.quote: The British ornithologist Graham S. Cowles instead found their skulls too dissimilar for them to be close relatives in 1987.

facts.statement: Julian Hume suggests the broad-billed parrot shares a common origin with other Mascarene parrots in the radiation of the tribe Psittaculini.
facts.quote: Hume has suggested that they have a common origin in the radiation of the tribe Psittaculini, basing this theory on morphological features and the fact that parrots from that group have managed to colonise many isolated islands in the Indian Ocean.

facts.statement: The broad-billed parrot possessed a disproportionately large head and jaws with a skull flattened from top to bottom, distinguishing it from other Mascarene parrots.
facts.quote: The broad-billed parrot had a disproportionately large head and jaws, and the skull was flattened from top to bottom, unlike in other Mascarene parrots.

facts.statement: Ridges on the skull indicate that the broad-billed parrot had a distinct frontal crest of feathers that was firmly attached and could not be raised or lowered, unlike in cockatoos.
facts.quote: Ridges on the skull indicate that its distinct frontal crest of feathers was firmly attached, and that the bird, unlike cockatoos, could not raise or lower it.

facts.statement: Measurements of early known bones show the mandible was 65–78 mm long and 65 mm wide, the femur was 58–63 mm long, the tibia was 88–99 mm long, and the metatarsus was 35 mm long.
facts.quote: Measurements of some of the first known bones show that the mandible was 65–78 mm in length, 65 mm in width, the femur was 58–63 mm in length, the tibia was 88–99 mm, and the metatarsus 35 mm.

facts.statement: Subfossil evidence indicates males measured 55–65 cm in length while females measured 45–55 cm.
facts.quote: Subfossils show that the males were larger, measuring 55–65 cm to the females' 45–55 cm.

facts.statement: The sexual dimorphism in skull size between males and females is the largest among all parrots.
facts.quote: The sexual dimorphism in size between male and female skulls is the largest among parrots.

facts.statement: The head was evidently blue, and research suggests the beak may have been red with greyish or blackish plumage, a pattern found in other Psittaculini members.
facts.quote: The head was evidently blue, and in 2007, Hume suggested the beak may have been red, and the rest of the plumage greyish or blackish, which also occurs in other members of Psittaculini.

facts.statement: Many authors, including the Newton brothers, inferred the bird was flightless based on the apparent short wings and large size in the 1601 sketch, though this is debated.
facts.quote: The Newton brothers and many authors after them inferred that it was flightless, due to the apparent short wings and large size shown in the 1601 Gelderland sketch.

facts.statement: Analysis of the underlying pencil sketch suggests the wings were not particularly short but appeared broad like forest-adapted species, with a large alula characteristic of slow-flying birds.
facts.quote: According to Hume, the underlying pencil sketch actually shows that the wings are not particularly short. They appear broad, as they commonly are in forest-adapted species, and the alula appears large, a feature of slow-flying birds.

facts.statement: Historical accounts state the bird could fly with difficulty, and illustrations show it perched on trees, which is improbable for a flightless bird.
facts.quote: Furthermore, Hoffman's account states that it could fly, albeit with difficulty, and the first published illustration shows the bird on top of a tree, an improbable position for a flightless bird.

facts.statement: The broad-billed parrot likely ate hard seeds from various Mauritian plants such as Latania loddigesii, Mimusops maxima, Sideroxylon grandiflorum, Diospyros egrettorium, and Pandanus utilis.
facts.quote: Many types of palms and palm-like plants on Mauritius produce hard seeds that the broad-billed parrot may have eaten, including Latania loddigesii, Mimusops maxima, Sideroxylon grandiflorum, Diospyros egrettorium, and Pandanus utilis.

facts.statement: In 2020, Joanna K. Carpenter and colleagues suggested the broad-billed parrot was an important seed disperser capable of destroying large seeds found low in the Mascarene flora.
facts.quote: The biologist Joanna K. Carpenter and colleagues stated in 2020 that extinct Mascarene birds like the broad-billed parrot, the dodo, and the Rodrigues solitaire could only reach seeds at low heights, and were therefore probably important seed dispersers, able to destroy the largest seeds among the Mascarene flora.

facts.statement: Holyoak argued based on radiographs that the broad-billed parrot had a weakly constructed mandible and likely fed on soft fruits instead of hard seeds.
facts.quote: On the basis of radiographs, Holyoak claimed that the mandible of the broad-billed parrot was weakly constructed and suggested that it would have fed on soft fruits rather than hard seeds.

facts.statement: In 2007, Hume noted the broad-billed parrot's mandible morphology resembled the hyacinth macaw's, suggesting it likely cracked open palm nuts.
facts.quote: Hume pointed out in 2007 that the mandible morphology of the broad-billed parrot is comparable to that of the largest living parrot, the hyacinth macaw, which cracks open palm nuts with ease. It is therefore probable that the broad-billed parrot fed in the same manner.

facts.statement: The broad-billed parrot is believed to have gone extinct by the 1680s due to large-scale harvesting of its palm food sources.
facts.quote: The bird is believed to have become extinct by the 1680s, when the palms it may have sustained itself on were harvested on a large scale.

facts.statement: Hume stated in 2007 that the broad-billed parrot's poor flight, large size, and tameness made it easy prey for sailors and vulnerable to introduced crab-eating macaques and rats.
facts.quote: Because of its poor flying ability, large size and possible island tameness, Hume stated in 2007 the broad-billed parrot was easy prey for sailors who visited Mauritius, and their nests would have been extremely vulnerable to predation by introduced crab-eating macaques and rats.

facts.statement: The IUCN status system lists the extinction year of Lophopsittacus mauritianus as 1693.
facts.quote: extinct: 1693

facts.statement: The broad-billed parrot is classified in the kingdom Animalia, phylum Chordata, class Aves, order Psittaciformes, family Psittacidae, and subfamily Psittacinae.
facts.quote: regnum: Animalia phylum: Chordata classis: Aves ordo: Psittaciformes familia: Psittacidae subfamilia: Psittacinae

facts.statement: A synonym for the broad-billed parrot is Psittacus mauritianus, originally described by Owen in 1866.
facts.quote: synonyms: Psittacus mauritianus Owen, 1866

facts.statement: The species was first scientifically described from a subfossil mandible in 1866, but linked to ancient accounts only after a 1601 sketch matching the fossils and descriptions was rediscovered.
facts.quote: Fue descrito científicamente por primera vez a partir de una mandíbula subfósil en 1866, pero no se vinculó con los relatos antiguos hasta el redescubrimiento de un detallado boceto de 1601 que coincidía tanto con los subfósiles como con las descripciones.

facts.statement: The broad-billed parrot had a large head relative to its body and a well-defined crest of feathers on the front of its head.
facts.quote: La cabeza del loro de pico ancho era grande en proporción al cuerpo, y tenía una cresta de plumas bien definida en la parte frontal de la cabeza.

facts.statement: The broad-billed parrot possessed a very large beak comparable in size to the hyacinth macaw, allowing it to break hard seeds.
facts.quote: Poseía un pico muy grande, comparable en tamaño al del guacamayo jacinto, lo que le habría permitido romper semillas duras.

facts.statement: Fossil bones indicate the broad-billed parrot exhibited greater sexual dimorphism in body and head size than any living parrot species.
facts.quote: Sus huesos indican que la especie exhibía un mayor dimorfismo sexual en tamaño corporal y tamaño de la cabeza que cualquier loro actual.

facts.statement: It is believed the broad-billed parrot had difficulty flying but was not flightless.
facts.quote: Se cree que volaba con dificultad, pero no era ápteno.

facts.statement: A contemporary description indicates the broad-billed parrot had multiple colors, including a blue head and possibly a red body and beak.
facts.quote: Una descripción contemporánea indica que tenía varios colores, incluida cabeza azul y quizá cuerpo y pico rojos.

facts.statement: The species went extinct in the late period due to deforestation, predation by introduced invasive species, and possibly hunting.
facts.quote: La especie se extinguió en algún momento a fines del debido a la deforestación, la depredación por especies invasoras introducidas y, posiblemente, la caza.

facts.statement: In 1987, British ornithologist Graham S. Cowles found the skulls were too distinct to be closely related to other species.
facts.quote: En cambio, el ornitólogo británico Graham S. Cowles halló en 1987 que sus cráneos eran demasiado distintos para ser parientes cercanos.

facts.statement: Hume suggested these parrots share a common origin in the evolutionary radiation of the tribe Psittaculini based on morphology and colonization of many Indian Ocean islands.
facts.quote: Hume sugirió que comparten un origen común en la radiación evolutiva de la tribu Psittaculini, basándose en la morfología y en que sus miembros colonizaron muchas islas del Índico.

facts.statement: Lophopsittacus mauritianus had disproportionately large heads and jaws with a dorsoventrally flattened skull compared to other Mascarene parrots.
facts.quote: El loro de pico ancho tenía cabeza y mandíbulas desproporcionadamente grandes, y el cráneo estaba aplanado dorsoventralmente, a diferencia de otros loros mascareños.

facts.statement: Its frontal crest was firmly anchored to the skull and could not be raised or lowered, unlike cockatoos.
facts.quote: Las crestas en el cráneo indican que su distintiva cresta frontal estaba firmemente anclada y que, a diferencia de las cacatúas, no podía alzarla o bajarla.

facts.statement: The wide posterior border of the mandibular symphysis indicates that the lower jaw was comparatively broad.
facts.quote: El ancho del borde posterior de la sínfisis mandibular (donde se unen las dos hemimandíbulas) indica que la mandíbula era comparativamente ancha.

facts.statement: Measurements of early known bones indicate the jaw was long and wide, the femur was long, the tibia was long, and the metatarsus was long.
facts.quote: Medidas de algunos de los primeros huesos conocidos indican que la mandíbula medía de largo, de ancho; el fémur, ; la tibia, ; y el metatarso, .

facts.statement: The sternum was relatively reduced in size.
facts.quote: El esternón estaba relativamente reducido.

facts.statement: Subfossils show that males were larger, measuring between while females measured between.
facts.quote: Los subfósiles muestran que los machos eran mayores, midiendo frente a en las hembras.

facts.statement: The sexual size dimorphism between male and female skulls is the greatest among parrots.
facts.quote: El dimorfismo sexual en tamaño entre cráneos de machos y hembras es el mayor entre los loros.

facts.statement: While differences in the rest of the skeleton were less pronounced, the total sexual dimorphism was greater than in any living parrot.
facts.quote: Las diferencias en el resto del esqueleto son menos pronunciadas; aun así, el dimorfismo total era mayor que en cualquier loro viviente.

facts.statement: The 1598 voyage report by van Neck, published in 1601, contains the first illustration of the parrot with a foot described as having two or three colors.
facts.quote: El informe del viaje de van Neck en 1598, publicado en 1601, contiene la primera ilustración del loro con el pie «de dos o tres colores».

facts.statement: In 1987, Hume proposed that, in addition to size dimorphism, the sexes might have had different colors, which could explain discrepancies in accounts.
facts.quote: En 1987 Hume también propuso que, además del dimorfismo de tamaño, los sexos podrían haber tenido colores diferentes, lo que explicaría discrepancias en los relatos.

facts.statement: The head was evidently blue, and in 2007 Hume suggested the beak might have been red while the rest of the plumage was grayish or blackish, as in other Psittaculini.
facts.quote: La cabeza era evidentemente azul y, en 2007, Hume sugirió que el pico pudo ser rojo y el resto del plumaje grisáceo o negruzco, como en otros Psittaculini.

facts.statement: Hume reinterpreted Hoffman's account and suggested the bird could have been vividly colored with a red body, blue head, and red beak, as illustrated in the work.
facts.quote: Hume reinterpretó acorde el relato de Hoffman y sugirió que pudo haber sido vistosamente coloreada con cuerpo rojo, cabeza azul y pico rojo; así se ilustró en el trabajo.

facts.statement: Possible iridescent or shiny feathers that change with the angle of light may have created the impression of even more colors.
facts.quote: Posibles plumas iridiscentes o brillantes que cambian según el ángulo de la luz pudieron dar impresión de aún más colores.

facts.statement: In 2017, Australian ornithologist Joseph M. Forshaw agreed the beak was red (at least in males) but interpreted Hoffman's account as a plainer overall coloration, brownish-red with a pale grayish-blue head, similar to the Mascarene parrot.
facts.quote: El ornitólogo australiano Joseph M. Forshaw coincidió en 2017 en que el pico era rojo (al menos en machos), pero interpretó el relato de Hoffman como una coloración general más sobria, pardo-rojiza, con cabeza azul grisácea pálida, similar a la del loro mascareño.

facts.statement: Although it may have fed on the ground and flown clumsily, its short and robust tarsometatarsus implies certain arboreal traits.
facts.quote: Aunque pudo alimentarse en el suelo y volar con torpeza, su tarsometatarso (hueso de la parte baja de la pierna) era corto y robusto, lo que implica ciertos rasgos arbóreos.

facts.statement: The Newton brothers and many authors inferred it was flightless due to apparently short wings and large size in the 1601 sketch.
facts.quote: Los hermanos Newton y muchos autores infirieron que era ápteno por las alas aparentemente cortas y el gran tamaño en el boceto de 1601.

facts.statement: According to Hume, the underlying pencil drawing shows the wings are not particularly short: they appear broad, as in forest-adapted species, and the alula appears large, a trait of slow-flying birds.
facts.quote: Según Hume, el dibujo a lápiz subyacente muestra que las alas no son particularmente cortas: parecen anchas, como en especies adaptadas a bosques, y el álula parece grande, rasgo de aves de vuelo lento.

facts.statement: Its keeled sternum was reduced but not enough to prevent flight, as seen in Cyanoramphus, and even the kākāpō, with a vestigial keel, can glide.
facts.quote: Su quilla esternal estaba reducida, pero no lo suficiente para impedir el vuelo, como también ocurre en los Cyanoramphus, y hasta el kākāpō, con quilla vestigial, puede planear.

facts.statement: Hoffman's account notes it could fly, albeit with difficulty, and the first published illustration shows it high in a tree, an unlikely position for a flightless bird.
facts.quote: El relato de Hoffman señala que podía volar, aunque con dificultad, y la primera ilustración publicada lo muestra en lo alto de un árbol, posición poco probable para un ave áptera.

facts.statement: The broad-billed parrot may have been nearly flightless behaviorally, like the extinct Norfolk Island kākā.
facts.quote: El loro de pico ancho pudo haber sido casi ápteno en términos conductuales, como el extinto kākā de la isla Norfolk.

facts.statement: Sexual size dimorphism in the beak may have affected its behavior; such dimorphism is common in other parrots like the palm cockatoo and New Zealand kākā.
facts.quote: El dimorfismo sexual en tamaño del pico pudo afectar su comportamiento. Dicho dimorfismo es común en otros loros, como la cacatúa palmera y el kākā de Nueva Zelanda.

facts.statement: When this occurs, sexes prefer foods of different sizes, males use the beak in rituals, or sexes have specialized roles in nesting and parenting.
facts.quote: Cuando ocurre, los sexos prefieren alimentos de diferente tamaño, los machos usan el pico en rituales o los sexos tienen roles especializados en nidificación y crianza.

facts.statement: Similarly, the large difference in head size may have reflected the ecology of each sex, though it is impossible to determine how.
facts.quote: Del mismo modo, la gran diferencia de tamaño de la cabeza puede haberse reflejado en la ecología de cada sexo, aunque es imposible determinar cómo.

facts.statement: In 1953, Japanese ornithologist Masauji Hachisuka suggested the broad-billed parrot was nocturnal, like the kākāpō and the night parrot, two current terrestrial parrots.
facts.quote: En 1953, el ornitólogo japonés Masauji Hachisuka sugirió que el loro de pico ancho era nocturno, como el kākāpō y el loro nocturno, dos loros terrestres actuales.

facts.statement: Contemporary accounts do not corroborate this, and the orbits are similar in size to other large diurnal parrots.
facts.quote: Los relatos contemporáneos no lo corroboran y las órbitas son de tamaño similar al de otros loros grandes diurnos.

facts.statement: It probably nested in tree or rock cavities, like the Cuban amazon.
facts.quote: Probablemente anidaba en cavidades de árboles o rocas, como la amazona cubana.

facts.statement: The terms 'crow' or 'raven' may refer to its harsh call, behavior, or dark plumage.
facts.quote: Los términos «cuervo» o «raven» pueden aludir a su llamada áspera, su comportamiento o su plumaje oscuro.

facts.statement: The broad-billed parrot coexisted with other recently extinct Mauritian birds such as the dodo, red rail, grey parrot, Mauritius blue pigeon, Mauritius nightjar, Mauritius teal, and Mauritius night heron.
facts.quote: El loro de pico ancho convivió con otras aves mauricianas extintas recientemente como el dodo, el rálido rojo, la cotorra gris mascareña, la paloma azul de Mauricio, el autillo de Mauricio, la focha mascareña, el ganso de Mauricio, la cerceta mascareña y la garceta nocturna de Mauricio.

facts.statement: Extinct reptiles included the saddle-back and dome-headed giant tortoises of Mauritius, the giant Mauritian skink, and the Red Island digging boa.
facts.quote: Los reptiles extintos incluyen las tortugas gigantes de Mauricio de caparazón en silla y en domo, el escinco gigante mauriciano y la boa excavadora de la Isla Redonda.

facts.statement: The small Mauritian flying fox and the shell Tropidophora carinata lived in Mauritius and Réunion but went extinct on both islands.
facts.quote: El zorro volador pequeño de Mauricio y el caracol Tropidophora carinata vivían en Mauricio y Reunión pero se extinguieron en ambas islas.

facts.statement: Before human arrival, Mauritius was completely covered by forests, almost all lost to deforestation.
facts.quote: Antes de la llegada humana, Mauricio estaba completamente cubierto por bosques, casi todos perdidos por la deforestación.

facts.statement: A 1602 account by Dutch sailor Reyer Cornelisz was traditionally interpreted as the only contemporary mention of size differences, listing 'large and small Indian crows'.
facts.quote: Un relato de 1602 del marinero neerlandés Reyer Cornelisz se interpretó tradicionalmente como la única mención contemporánea de diferencias de tamaño, listando «cuervos indios grandes y pequeños».

facts.statement: A complete transcription published in 2003 showed a comma was misplaced in the English translation: 'large and small' referred to 'field chickens', possibly the red rail and Cheke's lesser rail.
facts.quote: La transcripción completa publicada en 2003 mostró que una coma se había colocado mal en la traducción inglesa: «grandes y pequeños» se refería a «gallinas del campo», posiblemente el rálido rojo y el menor rálido de Cheke.

facts.statement: There has been confusion regarding the coloration of the broad-billed parrot.
facts.quote: Ha habido confusión sobre la coloración del loro de pico ancho.

facts.statement: Hume's 2003 examination of the diary revealed only a description of the dodo.
facts.quote: El examen del diario por Hume (2003) reveló solo una descripción del dodo.

facts.statement: Japanese ornithologist Masauji Hachisuka suggested the broad-billed parrot was nocturnal, like the kākāpō and night parrot, two current terrestrial parrots.
facts.quote: El ornitólogo japonés Masauji Hachisuka sugirió que el loro de pico ancho era nocturno, como el kākāpō y el loro nocturno, dos loros terrestres actuales.

facts.statement: Morphologically similar parrots, such as the hyacinth macaw, are ground-dwelling birds that consume very hard palm nuts.
facts.quote: Los guacamayos Anodorhynchus, habituales en el suelo, consumen nueces de palmera muy duras.

facts.statement: In Mauritius, the parrot likely ate hard seeds from many local plants, including Latania loddigesii, Mimusops maxima, Sideroxylon grandiflorum, Diospyros egrettorium, and Pandanus utilis.
facts.quote: En Mauricio, muchas palmeras y plantas afines producen semillas duras que pudo comer, incluyendo Latania loddigesii, Mimusops maxima, Sideroxylon grandiflorum, Diospyros egrettorium y Pandanus utilis.

facts.statement: The parrot and other extinct Mascarene birds, like the dodo and Rodrigues solitaire, could only reach seeds at low heights and were likely important seed predators capable of destroying the largest plants in the Mascarene flora.
facts.quote: El loro de pico ancho y otras aves mascareñas extintas, como el dodo y el solitario de Rodrigues, solo podían alcanzar semillas a baja altura y probablemente fueron importantes depredadores de semillas capaces de destruir las más grandes de la flora mascareña.

facts.statement: Based on X-rays, Holyoak claimed the parrot's jaw was weakly constructed and suggested it fed on soft fruits rather than hard seeds.
facts.quote: Basado en radiografías, Holyoak afirmó que la mandíbula del loro de pico ancho estaba débilmente construida y sugirió que se alimentaría de frutos blandos más que de semillas duras.

facts.statement: Holyoak attributed the weak jaw to internal trabeculae that were widely spaced, a wide upper maxilla relative to narrow palatines, and the absence of a preserved upper rostrum.
facts.quote: Como evidencia señaló trabéculas internas muy espaciadas, maxila superior ancha frente a palatinos estrechos y la ausencia de rostro superior preservado, que atribuyó a su delicadeza.

facts.statement: Ornithologist George A. Smith argued that the four genera Holyoak used as examples of strong jaws actually have weak jaws in life and that the cited morphologies do not indicate strength.
facts.quote: El ornitólogo George A. Smith señaló que los cuatro géneros usados por Holyoak como «mandíbulas fuertes» (Cyanorhamphus, Melopsittacus, Neophema y Psephotus) en realidad tienen mandíbulas débiles en vida, y que las morfologías citadas no indican fuerza.

facts.statement: Hume (2007) noted that the parrot's jaw morphology is comparable to that of the largest living parrot, the hyacinth macaw, which easily cracks open palm nuts, suggesting it likely fed in a similar way.
facts.quote: Hume (2007) señaló que la morfología mandibular del loro de pico ancho es comparable a la del mayor loro viviente, el guacamayo jacinto, que abre nueces de palmera con facilidad. Por tanto, probablemente se alimentaba de forma similar.

facts.statement: Yamashita suggested that the abundant Cylindraspis tortoises and dodos performed the same function in Mauritius and that the parrot, with its macaw-like beak, depended on them to obtain clean seeds.
facts.quote: Yamashita también sugirió que las abundantes tortugas Cylindraspis y los dodos cumplían la misma función en Mauricio y que el loro de pico ancho, con su pico «tipo guacamayo», dependía de ellos para obtener semillas limpias.

facts.statement: The genus Lophopsittacus belongs to the parent group Psittaculini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Psittaculini

facts.statement: The genus Lophopsittacus is classified in the family Psittaculidae.
facts.quote: Family: Psittaculidae

facts.statement: The genus Lophopsittacus lived during the Holocene, from 0.0117 to 0 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Holocene to Holocene (0.0117 to 0 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Lophopsittacus was named by Newton in 1876.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Lophopsittacus (genus), Newton 1876
